title: A Look at Alone Against Fear
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IB_3oFDAULc

Daniel (@dungeondive) takes a look at Alone Against Fear, Andrea Sfiligoi's solo survival-horror spin-off of Four Against Darkness. He liked but never loved the parent game — steering a four-hero party left him invested in no one — and he's currently prizing low-overhead games, having failed to get five boxes of Siege of the Citadel to the table. Here you play one survivor in a town where the supernatural has broken loose: no phones, no internet, and gremlins crash cars, so you walk. The campaign goal is to close seven Hell Gates; he has closed one.

Character creation takes minutes: a name, Sanity and Life, two skills (he rolled Faith and Slippery), a weapon from a table running baseball bat to authentic samurai sword, and two items. Each session is one pass through a freshly generated town, rolling down nested charts sector by sector until you land in a clinic, sewer, cemetery or special event. Wounds and madness can be traded for persistent scars, phobias and eating disorders.

His character Barry Bobby Burnside, stranded in mid-90s Tulare, California en route to an arcade job, fought a giant sewer rat, learned Gate Arcane from a holy book, fled a slasher called Rabbit Face and defended a church against zombies. What it evokes is less Resident Evil than Dreamcast B-grade survival horror — Illbleed and Blue Stinger — awkward, weird and charming for it. The Village of the Living Dolls hex-crawl supplement is next.

----

Daniel says Alone Against Fear feels like a pen-and-paper Illbleed. Which solo game has best captured the flavour of a specific video game era for you?
